<content>1: ---
2: title: use server
3: description: Learn how to use the use server directive to execute code on the server.
4: ---
5: 
6: The `use server` directive designates a function or file to be executed on the **server side**. It can be used at the top of a file to indicate that all functions in the file are server-side, or inline at the top of a function to mark the function as a [Server Function](https://19.react.dev/reference/rsc/server-functions). This is a React feature.
7: 
8: ## Using `use server` at the top of a file
9: 
10: The following example shows a file with a `use server` directive at the top. All functions in the file are executed on the server.
11: 
12: ```tsx filename="app/actions.ts" highlight={1} switcher
13: 'use server'
14: import { db } from '@/lib/db' // Your database client
15: 
16: export async function createUser(data: { name: string; email: string }) {
17:   const user = await db.user.create({ data })
18:   return user
19: }
20: ```
21: 
22: ```jsx filename="app/actions.js" highlight={1} switcher
23: 'use server'
24: import { db } from '@/lib/db' // Your database client
25: 
26: export async function createUser(data) {
27:   const user = await db.user.create({ data })
28:   return user
29: }
30: ```
31: 
32: ### Using Server Functions in a Client Component
33: 
34: To use Server Functions in Client Components you need to create your Server Functions in a dedicated file using the `use server` directive at the top of the file. These Server Functions can then be imported into Client and Server Components and executed.
35: 
36: Assuming you have a `fetchUsers` Server Function in `actions.ts`:
37: 
38: ```tsx filename="app/actions.ts" highlight={1} switcher
39: 'use server'
40: import { db } from '@/lib/db' // Your database client
41: 
42: export async function fetchUsers() {
43:   const users = await db.user.findMany()
44:   return users
45: }
46: ```
47: 
48: ```jsx filename="app/actions.js" highlight={1} switcher
49: 'use server'
50: import { db } from '@/lib/db' // Your database client
51: 
52: export async function fetchUsers() {
53:   const users = await db.user.findMany()
54:   return users
55: }
56: ```
57: 
58: Then you can import the `fetchUsers` Server Function into a Client Component and execute it on the client-side.
59: 
60: ```tsx filename="app/components/my-button.tsx" highlight={1,2,5} switcher
61: 'use client'
62: import { fetchUsers } from '../actions'
63: 
64: export default function MyButton() {
65:   return <button onClick={() => fetchUsers()}>Fetch Users</button>
66: }
67: ```
68: 
69: ```jsx filename="app/components/my-button.js" highlight={1,2,5} switcher
70: 'use client'
71: import { fetchUsers } from '../actions'
72: 
73: export default function MyButton() {
74:   return <button onClick={() => fetchUsers()}>Fetch Users</button>
75: }
76: ```
77: 
78: ## Using `use server` inline
79: 
80: In the following example, `use server` is used inline at the top of a function to mark it as a [Server Function](https://19.react.dev/reference/rsc/server-functions):
81: 
82: ```tsx filename="app/posts/[id]/page.tsx" switcher highlight={8}
83: import { EditPost } from './edit-post'
84: import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache'
85: 
86: export default async function PostPage({ params }: { params: { id: string } }) {
87:   const post = await getPost(params.id)
88: 
89:   async function updatePost(formData: FormData) {
90:     'use server'
91:     await savePost(params.id, formData)
92:     revalidatePath(`/posts/${params.id}`)
93:   }
94: 
95:   return <EditPost updatePostAction={updatePost} post={post} />
96: }
97: ```
98: 
99: ```jsx filename="app/posts/[id]/page.js" switcher highlight={8}

102: 
103: export default async function PostPage({ params }) {
104:   const post = await getPost(params.id)
105: 
106:   async function updatePost(formData) {

108:     await savePost(params.id, formData)
109:     revalidatePath(`/posts/${params.id}`)
110:   }
111: 
112:   return <EditPost updatePostAction={updatePost} post={post} />
113: }
114: ```
115: 
116: ## Security considerations
117: 
118: When using the `use server` directive, it's important to ensure that all server-side logic is secure and that sensitive data remains protected.
119: 
120: ### Authentication and authorization
121: 
122: Always authenticate and authorize users before performing sensitive server-side operations.
123: 
124: ```tsx filename="app/actions.ts" highlight={1,7,8,9,10} switcher
125: 'use server'
126: 
127: import { db } from '@/lib/db' // Your database client
128: import { authenticate } from '@/lib/auth' // Your authentication library
129: 
130: export async function createUser(
131:   data: { name: string; email: string },
132:   token: string
133: ) {
134:   const user = authenticate(token)
135:   if (!user) {
136:     throw new Error('Unauthorized')
137:   }
138:   const newUser = await db.user.create({ data })
139:   return newUser
140: }
141: ```

153:   }
154:   const newUser = await db.user.create({ data })
155:   return newUser
156: }
157: ```
